trig.name: Step chance and conditions
device: MIDI Control Center accepted the update file; the unit restarted by itself and played existing patterns as before.
Chance (Randomness) and conditions (Probability) on SEQ1 and SEQ2 worked, and survived a save and a power cycle.
The inverted form reads clearly on the display as n12.
The update file, which has one more data frame than Arturia's, was accepted; the unit runs and the mod works.
trig.unchecked: Not yet reported from a device: swing, drum shift, reverse and alternate direction, changing pattern while playing, copy project, and long use.
guide: What it adds
In the stock firmware, a step that is on plays each time the pattern comes round. The mod adds two ways to make a step play only some of the time:

list: A chance makes the step play at random, for example about half the times.
A condition makes the step play on fixed passes of the pattern. The result is the same each time you play it.

guide: A step has a chance or a condition, not both. Steps that you do not change play as before.
A pass is one time through the pattern. In a 16-step pattern, pass 1 is the first 16 steps after you press Play. Pass 2 is the next 16 steps.
The knob names do not match the functions. The Randomness knob sets the chance. The Probability knob sets the condition.

guide.alt: Hold a step that is on, then turn Randomness or Probability. The display shows the value.

guide: Set a chance

steps: Select the track: SEQ1, SEQ2 or DRUM.
On the DRUM track, select the pad.
Hold a step that is on.
Turn the Randomness knob while you hold the step.
Read the chance on the display, in percent.

guide: The step stays on after you release it.
A chance of 50 makes the step play about half the times it comes round. A chance of 25 makes it play about one time in four. The mod decides again each time the step comes round.
The chance has 21 values from 1 to 99. The values are closer together near 1 and near 99. One click of the knob moves to the next value.

guide.alt: The 21 chance values on a line from 0 to 100. The values are closer together at the two ends.

guide: To remove the chance, turn Randomness to the right until the display shows 100. A step with a chance of 100 is a normal step.
When you hold no step, the Randomness knob does its stock function.
Set a condition

steps: Select the track: SEQ1, SEQ2 or DRUM.
On the DRUM track, select the pad.
Hold a step that is on.
Turn the Probability knob while you hold the step.
Read the condition on the display.

guide: To remove the condition, turn Probability to the left until the display shows 1-1.
When you hold no step, the Probability knob does its stock function.
When you turn Probability to the right, the display shows the conditions in this order: 1-1, 1St, n1S, 1-2, 2-2, 1-3, n13, 2-3, n23, 3-3, n33, 1-4, n14, 2-4, n24, 3-4, n34, 4-4, n44.
How to read a condition

list: 1-1 is no condition. The step plays on each pass.
1St plays on pass 1 only.
n1S plays on each pass except pass 1.
A-B counts the passes in groups of B. The step plays on pass A of each group.
nAB is the opposite of A-B. The step plays on each pass except the pass that A-B plays on.

guide: For example, 1-2 plays on passes 1, 3, 5, 7 and so on. 4-4 plays on passes 4, 8, 12 and so on. n44 plays on passes 1, 2, 3, then 5, 6, 7.

guide.alt: A grid with one row for each condition and one column for each pass from 1 to 12. A filled square shows that the step plays.

table: not in the firmware: the same passes as 2-2
not in the firmware: the same passes as 1-2

guide: n12 and n22 are not in the firmware from version 1.3.2. n12 plays on the same passes as 2-2. n22 plays on the same passes as 1-2. The Probability knob steps over them.
Version 1.2.1 still shows n12 and n22. A step saved with n12 or n22 keeps it and plays as before.
Chance and condition on one step
A step keeps only the last of the two that you set.

list: If a step has a condition, Randomness shows 100. Turn Randomness to the left to set a chance. The chance replaces the condition.
If a step has a chance, Probability shows 1-1. Turn Probability to the right to set a condition. The condition replaces the chance.

guide: How the mod counts passes

list: The count starts at pass 1 when you press Play from stop.
The count starts at pass 1 again when the pattern changes.
SEQ1 and SEQ2 each count their own passes. Tracks of different lengths drift against each other, as in the stock firmware.
On the DRUM track, the step buttons show the steps of the selected pad. The chance and the condition that you set belong to that pad.
Each drum pad counts the passes of its own length.
In the alternate direction, one pass is the way there and the way back.

guide: Examples
A fill at the end of each fourth bar: set the steps of the fill to 4-4.

guide.alt: A 16-step drum part over 4 passes. The kick plays on each pass. The fill on steps 14, 15 and 16 plays on pass 4 only.

list: A phrase that is longer than the pattern: set some steps of a 16-step pattern to 1-2 and others to 2-2. The result is a 32-step phrase. With 1-4, 2-4, 3-4 and 4-4, the result is a 64-step phrase.
An intro that plays one time: set its steps to 1St.
A part that starts on the second pass: set its steps to n1S.
Hi-hats or ghost notes that change: set a chance from 50 to 75.

guide: Ratchets on DRUM steps
A ratchet makes a DRUM step play 2, 4 or 8 times inside its own length. On a 1/16 track, a ratchet of 2 gives a 1/32 roll. The step size of the track does not change.

steps: Select the DRUM track and the pad.
Hold a step that is on.
Touch the roller strip at a rate finer than the step size of the track.
Read the ratchet on the display: r 2, r 4 or r 8.

list: On a 1/16 track, 1/32 gives 2 hits.
On a 1/8 track, 1/16 gives 2 hits and 1/32 gives 4 hits.
On a 1/4 track, 1/8 gives 2 hits, 1/16 gives 4 hits and 1/32 gives 8 hits.

guide: To remove the ratchet, touch the strip at the rate of the track or a coarser rate. The display shows r 1.

list: Ratcheted steps light cyan, not purple.
Recording: when Record is on, a roll finer than the track marks each step in which the roll plays two or more hits.
All hits have the velocity of the step. The gate of the step applies to the gap between hits, at most 90 percent. Each hit ends before the next hit.
The mod decides a chance or a condition one time, for all hits of the step.
A drum pattern holds up to 96 ratchets. At the limit, the display shows FuL.
When you hold a drum step and turn Swing, the display shows the ratchet of the step. The swing does not change.
Ratchets do not play while the looper repeats steps.

guide: Step lights

list: A step with a chance blinks off one time each second.
A step with a condition blinks off two times in quick succession every two seconds.
A step with a ratchet blinks in cyan.
While you hold a step, its light does not blink.

guide: A step has a chance or a condition, not both. Thus a step never blinks in both ways.
Saving and copying

list: When you save the project, the mod saves the chances and the conditions with the pattern.
When you turn a step off, the step loses its chance or condition.
The stock functions that shift or copy steps also remove them.
When you copy a pattern or a project, the copy keeps them.
Arturia's firmware ignores them. After you go back to the stock firmware, a pattern saved with the mod plays each step that is on again.

trig.summary: Each SEQ1, SEQ2 and DRUM step can have a chance to play (hold the step, turn Randomness) or a condition such as every second pass (hold the step, turn Probability).
changes: Hold a step with a chance, a condition or a ratchet and turn Swing, Randomness or Probability only to look at the value: the step stays on when you release it. Before, a look without a change turned the step off. A plain step still goes off, as stock.
A press on a step that is on no longer removes its chance, condition or ratchet. Before, each new press of the step reset it to plainly on.
A step with a condition blinks off two times in quick succession every two seconds, in place of the long dark gap of 1.4.1. A step with a chance still blinks off one time each second.
The step lights blink at half the speed of 1.4.0: a chance blinks off one time each second, a condition goes off for half a second in every two seconds.
Step lights: a step with a chance blinks off two times each second, a step with a condition goes off for a quarter of each second. A ratcheted step blinks in cyan. A held step does not blink.
The Probability knob steps over n12 and n22. They play on the same passes as 2-2 and 1-2. A step saved with n12 or n22 keeps it and plays as before.

Recording: a hit recorded over a rolled step now always removes its ratchet. 1.3.0 followed only the roller's own hits, one of the ten places a recorded hit comes from; it was never installed on a device.

Ratchets on DRUM steps: a step can play 2, 4 or 8 times inside its own length. Hold a step and touch the roller strip at a rate finer than the track to set it, at the track's rate or coarser to clear it; recording a finer roll sets it too. Ratcheted steps light cyan. Up to 96 per drum pattern, saved with it.
Chance and conditions on DRUM steps too, set on the selected pad's steps and saved with the drum pattern. Each pad counts the passes of its own length. Copy project carries them.

Step conditions on SEQ1 and SEQ2: hold a step and turn Probability. 1-1 is none, 1St and n1S are first pass only and not first pass, A-B plays on pass A of every B, nAB on every pass but that one, for B up to 4.
The chance of a held step is now set with the Randomness knob. Probability is left as stock, kept for per-step conditions.
First version: per-step trigger chance, saved with the pattern.

dump.name: Bootloader dump
dump.summary: Sends the bootloader over USB MIDI when Probability is turned. A one-off tool, not for playing.
changes: Fix: 1.0.0 sent the dump out of the 5-pin MIDI output instead of USB. Now sent over USB, and a message the USB queue refuses is sent again.
